cart-summary.description: The order totals beside the cart: item count, subtotal, savings and total. It fills itself from the shopper's cart, so its table stays empty.
cart-summary.structureOnly: it reads the shopper's cart from the browser and prices it with the storefront's own scripts/data-mock.js, and it fills page markup with fixed class names (subtotal, savings, total) that a document table cannot hold.

featured-products.description: A row of four products on the home page, chosen by the storefront's catalog. It fills itself, so its table stays empty.
featured-products.structureOnly: it loads its products from the live catalog through the storefront's own scripts/services/catalog-service.js and scripts/auth.js, and it draws them into a products-container element a document table cannot hold.

filters-sidebar.description: The filter list beside the product list: categories, price and the catalog's own facets. It fills itself from the catalog, so its table stays empty.
filters-sidebar.structureOnly: it draws the facets the live catalog search returns into a dynamic-facets-container element, which a document table cannot hold; without it the block does nothing.

footer.description: The site footer: link columns, contact details and the legal line. The storefront adds it to every page itself, so it is not placed on pages.
footer.structureOnly: the storefront's scripts load it on every page from the block's own built-in markup (footer.html); its code only fixes link paths and reads nothing from a table.

fragment.description: Shows the content of another page in place, so one piece of content can be reused on many pages. Put a link to that page, or its path, in the single cell.
fragment.structureOnly: it fetches the linked page from the storefront and shows that page's content, and it imports the storefront's own scripts/utils.js and scripts/scripts.js, which only its own storefront has.

header.description: The site header: logo, search, navigation, account and cart. The storefront adds it to every page itself, so it is not placed on pages.
header.structureOnly: the storefront's scripts load it on every page from the block's own built-in markup (header.html), and it needs the signed-in shopper, the cart and live search from the storefront's own scripts.

inventory-status.description: Stock for one product at each warehouse, nearest first. The product page fills it, so its table stays empty.
inventory-status.structureOnly: it reads the product from a data-sku attribute the product page sets and loads its stock from the live store through the storefront's own scripts; an author cannot set that attribute in a document.

mini-cart.description: The cart drop-down that opens from the header cart icon, listing what the shopper has added. It fills itself from the cart, so its table stays empty.
mini-cart.structureOnly: it is part of the header, fills built-in markup (mini-cart-items, mini-cart-total) from the shopper's cart in the browser, and imports the storefront's own scripts/cart-manager.js.

pricing-display.description: A product's price for the shopper's pricing tier, with the volume price table. The product page fills it, so its table stays empty.
pricing-display.structureOnly: it reads the product from a data-sku attribute and price data the product page hands it in code, and returns at once without them; an author cannot set either in a document.

product-detail.description: The styles for the product page layout. It has no code of its own; the product page builds its markup.
product-detail.structureOnly: it has no JavaScript at all, only styles for markup (product-cookware-layout and its parts) that the product page's own script builds, so a table placed on a page shows nothing of it.

product-gallery.description: A product's main image, thumbnails and zoom. The product page fills it, so its table stays empty.
product-gallery.structureOnly: it reads the product from a data-sku attribute and image data the product page hands it in code, and returns at once without them; an author cannot set either in a document.

product-grid.description: The searchable, sortable product list with infinite scroll. It fills itself from the catalog, so its table stays empty.
product-grid.structureOnly: it loads products from the live catalog through the storefront's own scripts/services/catalog-service.js and scripts/auth.js, and draws them into a products-container element a document table cannot hold.

product-tile.description: One selectable product card, used inside the project builder. Code fills it, so it is not placed on pages by hand.
product-tile.structureOnly: its own code says it is controlled by JavaScript with live catalog data rather than author content: it builds an empty card and waits for another script to give it a product.

project-builder.description: The step-by-step project builder form that turns a few answers into a kit of materials. Its form is built in, so its table stays empty.
project-builder.structureOnly: it decorates a built-in form of radio buttons, inputs and steps (project-builder.html) that a document table cannot hold, and a separate wizard script runs it.

project-bundle.description: One generated kit of materials, with its items, quantities and total. The project builder fills it, so its table stays empty.
project-bundle.structureOnly: it reads the kit from a data-bundle attribute the project builder sets, and returns at once without it; an author cannot set that attribute in a document.

project-filter.description: A drop-down that narrows the catalog to one kind of project. Its list is built in, so its table stays empty.
project-filter.structureOnly: it works on a select list with fixed choices (project-filter.html), which a document table cannot hold, and keeps the choice in the browser.

tier-badge.description: A badge naming the signed-in shopper's pricing tier. It fills itself from the account, so its table stays empty.
tier-badge.structureOnly: it needs the signed-in shopper from the storefront's own scripts/auth.js, fills tier-label and savings-indicator elements a document table cannot hold, and resets its own classes.

user-menu.description: The account drop-down that opens from the header: sign in, or the shopper's name, company and account links. It fills itself, so its table stays empty.
user-menu.structureOnly: it is part of the header, switches between built-in signed-in and signed-out markup (user-menu.html), and imports the storefront's own scripts/auth.js and scripts/data-mock.js.

wizard-progress.description: The numbered step bar across the top of the project builder. Its steps are built in, so its table stays empty.
wizard-progress.structureOnly: it marks up built-in step markup (wizard-progress.html) that a document table cannot hold, and the project builder's script moves it from step to step.

wizard-sidebar.description: The project summary card beside the project builder, listing the choices made so far. It fills itself, so its table stays empty.
wizard-sidebar.structureOnly: its code does nothing; the project builder's script fills built-in markup (wizard-sidebar.html) that a document table cannot hold.

wizard-vertical-progress.description: A vertical list of steps with done, current and to-do marks. Code fills it, so its table stays empty.
wizard-vertical-progress.structureOnly: its own code says it is controlled by JavaScript, not author content: it clears its table and waits for another script to hand it the steps, and it imports the storefront's own scripts/icon-helper.js.
